source.title: Some unsolved problems in mathematics and computation

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer n, how many different polyominoes can be formed from n connected unit squares? The source frames this as asking for a general formula for the number of n-square polyominoes after listing the values 1, 1, 2, 5, 12, and 35 for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, and it explicitly states that no formula is known.

evidence.quote: How many different polynominoes can we form with n squares? # of squares 1 2 3 4 5 6 . . . n . . . # of polyominoes 1 1 2 5 12 35 . . . ?? . . . No formula is known!

accepted.question_text: When factoring a large composite integer, is brute-force search through possible divisors fundamentally necessary, or is there a method that avoids searching even when the search space is huge? The source motivates this by saying that one can divide by 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, and so on until a factor is found, but that this brute-force method is very slow for huge search spaces.

evidence.quote: One can divide by 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, . . . until one finds a factor. However, this method (brute force search) is very slow when the search space is huge. Is searching necessary? We don’t know.

accepted.question_text: For a graph with 100 nodes, can one determine whether it contains a clique of size 10 without relying on a search procedure that may take centuries of computer time? The source presents this as the question of whether searching is necessary for the clique-finding problem.

evidence.quote: For a graph with 100 nodes, finding whether it contains a clique of size 10 may take centuries of computer time by searching. Is searching necessary? We don’t know.

accepted.question_text: Is P equal to NP? In the source's terminology, P is the class of quickly solvable problems, such as multiplication, and NP is the class of quickly checkable problems, such as factoring or clique-finding. The source states the equivalent formulation as whether search problems can be solved without searching.

evidence.quote: P "polynomial time" Quickly solvable problems, such as multiplication. NP "nondeterministic polynomial time" Quickly checkable problems, such as factoring or clique-finding. Is P = NP? In other words, can we solve search problems without searching? Most people believe that P6=NP, but nobody knows for sure.

needs_review.question_text_raw: One of the problems, called the Poincaré Conjecture, has been solved since then.

evidence.quote: One of the problems, called the Poincaré Conjecture, has been solved since then.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The other six remain open problems.

evidence.quote: The other six remain open problems. My favorite one is the so called P versus NP problem.
